Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Worsening red, sore, very itchy, dry skin rash over chest, hands, arms, especially antecubital fossae for “the past few days.”  
  • No new topical products, foods, or environmental exposures reported.

- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Chronic eczema history; current flare described as “way worse” than usual in last few days.  
  • No weeping or exudate; some cracks present.

- ENT symptoms: patient specifically denied or did not report
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: not reported  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: not reported  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: not reported  
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: not reported  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea: breathing “OK,” uses blue inhaler only with asthma flare  
  • Swelling of lips/tongue/uvula/face: none reported  
  • Ear pain/hearing changes, neck swelling/pain: none reported

- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • Long-standing eczema; prior topical hydrocortisone (patient unsure of name) and emollients (Diprobase, Dermol).  
  • Tried OTC cetirizine antihistamine previously without benefit.  
  • Asthma with intermittent salbutamol inhaler use; no recent exacerbation.

- Allergies: No known drug or food allergies.

- Current medications:
  • Diprobase cream – dose/route/frequency not documented (topical emollient).  
  • Dermol/“dermal” soap substitute – dose/route/frequency not documented (topical).  
  • Hydrocortisone topical steroid – dose/frequency not documented.  
  • Salbutamol inhaler – dose/frequency not documented (PRN).  

- Social context: Patient at home in London; consultation conducted in private.

Objective:
- Observable swelling/distribution: Patient reports diffuse erythematous, dry, cracked patches on chest, arms, hands, most severe in antecubital fossae; no visible examination by clinician (video only).  
- Airway/breathing: No breathing difficulty reported; uses salbutamol only during flares.  
- Mental status: Alert, oriented, conversational.  
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.  
- Accompaniment: None mentioned.

Assessment:
- Extensive eczema flare with increased pruritus and erythema; no evidence of secondary infection or ENT-related airway involvement.  
- Asthma well controlled; no current respiratory compromise.  
- Possible need for stronger topical steroid and non-sedating antihistamine.

Plan:
- Medications prescribed:
  • Fexofenadine (antihistamine) – dose/route/frequency not documented; sent to Boots pharmacy.  
  • Betnovate (topical potent corticosteroid) – apply thin layer (“one fingertip unit”) twice daily to affected areas for 2 weeks.  
- Continue current emollients (Diprobase, Dermol).  
- Stop/replace weak hydrocortisone with Betnovate during treatment course.  
- Follow-up: If no improvement or any adverse reaction within 2 weeks, patient to contact clinic sooner; routine review after 2 weeks otherwise.  
- Red-flag advice: Seek medical attention if rash worsens markedly, signs of infection (weeping, pus, fever) appear, or any new symptoms of swelling, breathing difficulty, throat tightening, or facial/lip/tongue swelling develop.  
- Prescription logistics: Sent electronically to Boots pharmacy for collection.  
- Education: Use very small amounts of Betnovate; continue regular emollient use; monitor skin changes.

Quality checks:
• Missing but expected elements: Objective physical examination (skin & ENT), vitals, detailed dosing for new medications, documentation of asthma control metrics, confirmation of auto-injector availability (not relevant now but expected for potential allergy patients).  
• Internal conflicts: Patient reports mother has “hypothyroidism;” physician restated as “hyperthyroidism” – conflict noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear overall; occasional overlaps and minor inaudible words but did not obscure clinical content.
